comparison: Both evaluate technical performance and data quality (C3, C30, C31). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of reproducibility and coverage; peer reviewers accepted the technical approach without criticism, with Reviewer 1 stating 'the results are convincing.'

Both address validation against known origins (C32, C33, C34). OpenEval emphasizes strong correspondence with known origins as evidence for method validity; peer reviewers accepted this validation, with Reviewer 2 noting similarity in top 500 binding sites.

Both evaluate evidence linking Mcm abundance to replication activity (C4, C35, C36, C41). OpenEval finds converging evidence SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting that group-based analysis prevents concluding all 1600 sites act as origins.

Both assess nucleosome positioning data (C5, C42, C43). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of orthogonal methods; peer reviewers accepted findings with Reviewer 1 noting sites are 'for the most part free of nucleosomes.' Peer review also includes C48 (abrupt transition) not emphasized in OpenEval's nucleosome result.

Both evaluate ACS motif enrichment (C6, C53, C54, C55). OpenEval finds systematic enrichment SUPPORTED with detailed PWM analysis; peer reviewers accepted findings, with Reviewer 1 noting 'presence of ARS consensus sequences' as consistent with origins.

Both assess directional Mcm loading (C57, C58, C76, C77). OpenEval finds 77% downstream positioning SUPPORTED and notes technical advance over ChIP; peer reviewers accepted the observation while acknowledging Mcm mobility as a caveat but not disputing the finding itself.

Both evaluate GC skew patterns (C7, C64, C65, C67). OpenEval emphasizes midpoint reversal and requirement for precise alignment; peer reviewers accepted GC skew as characteristic of replication origins, with both reviewers noting this feature.

Both address detailed GC skew patterns (C80, C81). OpenEval explicitly discusses midpoint reversal and mechanistic insight; peer reviewers implicitly accepted this detailed pattern as part of overall GC skew analysis without dispute.

Both evaluate the central conclusion about ~5500 origins (C8, C68, C85). OpenEval finds convergence across multiple methods SUPPORTED; peer reviewers strongly affirmed this, with editor stating 'convincing evidence' and Reviewer 2 noting the work 'greatly broadens the number of sites.'

Both assess the speculative claim about initiation in every intergenic region (C9, C72). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting it goes beyond direct demonstration; peer reviewers also rated UNCERTAIN, accepting broader origin distribution but not explicitly endorsing this extreme interpretation.

Both evaluate reconciliation with prior single-molecule studies (C10, C74, C75). OpenEval finds the calculation SUPPORTED and provides coherent explanation; peer reviewers accepted this reconciliation, with Reviewer 1 noting consistency with published single molecule results.

Both assess comparative conclusion about yeast vs. human origins (C11). OpenEval finds the inference SUPPORTED based on dispersed origins in yeast; peer reviewers accepted this, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging 'previously unappreciated versatility' while noting sequence specificity still distinguishes yeast.

Both evaluate mechanistic model of single double hexamers and population-level licensing (C44, C45, C82). OpenEval finds observation SUPPORTED with logical inference; peer reviewers accepted without challenge, noting Mcm mobility as caveat but not disputing the single-hexamer observation or model.

Both address gene orientation preferences (C50, C51). OpenEval includes these in genomic localization patterns result; peer reviewers accepted these observations as consistent with previous reports without challenge.

Minimal overlap on C48 (abrupt transition at rank 5000). OpenEval includes this in genomic localization result as distinguishing functional origins; peer review groups it with nucleosome positioning findings.

OpenEval evaluates technical validation linking fragment size to cryo-EM data (C28, C29) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this technical detail was not explicitly discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates ChEC method capabilities (C27) as SUPPORTED, noting superior resolution over ChIP. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers accepted the method generally but did not separately evaluate this methodological claim.
OpenEval evaluates background knowledge about Mcm sliding and loading (C59, C60) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these are cited caveats rather than new findings.
OpenEval evaluates limitation in ACS identification (C79) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation; this contextualizes ACS analysis but was not separately discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates alternative interpretations and assumptions (C69, C71) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these represent analytical assumptions not explicitly discussed by reviewers.
OpenEval evaluates speculative mechanisms for GC skew persistence (C83, C84) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these hypotheses were not separately assessed by reviewers.
OpenEval evaluates extensive background knowledge (C1, C12-C25) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers did not separately assess background claims.
OpenEval evaluates reference to authors' prior work (C2) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation; this establishes methodological foundation but was not separately discussed.
OpenEval evaluates mechanistic basis for GC skew (C62, C63) as SUPPORTED background knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation; this contextualizes analysis but was not separately assessed.

OpenEval evaluates potential explanations for exceptions to downstream loading (C78) as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation; this represents acknowledgment of limitations not separately discussed by reviewers.

Peer reviewers identified critical weakness in group-based analysis preventing conclusion that all 1600 sites act as origins (C37, C38, C39, C40 not in peer result but related to replication activity claims). OpenEval R2 addresses overlapping claims (C4, C35-C41) but rates SUPPORTED, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to analytical limitations.
